title: A Extraction for the Contact
premise: Noor Nakamura, a ghost-assigned hostage negotiator whose one public failure still haunts the record, is approached by a stranger claiming Noor once saved their life — a favor Noor has no memory of. The debt comes due: the stranger, Elias Voss, is a courier carrying evidence that three governments plan to bury a massacre before an upcoming summit, and he needs Noor to broker his extraction across borders that all want him silent. As Noor pieces together the missing memory — a night they were made to forget by the same agency that erased them from every record — they realize their invisibility was engineered, and their forgotten favor was the price of their own survival. Hunted by an assassin who knew Noor's erased past intimately, Noor must smuggle Voss and the truth through three governments' blockades to the summit itself, where exposing the massacre means also exposing what was done to them. In the end, Noor trades their last shred of anonymity for the truth, choosing at last to be seen.
about_author: Petra Almeida is a former crisis-line counselor who spent six years listening to people talk their way out of the worst nights of their lives. She writes thrillers about the quiet machinery of memory and the people who operate it.

chapters.title: The Unattributed
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Opening on a midnight negotiation no agency will claim, establishing Noor's skill and their deliberate erasure from official records. The emotional beat is controlled loneliness — competence as camouflage.

chapters.title: A Favor Never Given
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A stranger, Elias Voss, appears at Noor's apartment insisting Noor saved his life years ago; Noor remembers nothing. The beat is uncanny disruption — the first crack in a carefully invisible life.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Voss reveals he carries encrypted proof of a pre-summit cover-up and needs extraction across three borders. Noor refuses, but finds a photograph of themselves in his effects — dated the night of their only failure. Beat: dread taking root.

chapters.title: The Board Still Shows One Loss
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter in Noor's POV reconstructing the failed negotiation in Lisbon — the hostage who died, the official record, the gaps in Noor's own recollection of that night. Beat: grief sharpening into suspicion.

chapters.title: Three Flags
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Noor and a foreign ministry fixer, Adeyemi, tasked with making Voss disappear quietly. The reader learns the scale of the conspiracy. Beat: the walls closing in from above.

chapters.title: The Man Who Knew Her Name Before It Was Erased
chapters.summary: Introduce the assassin, Sable, in her own POV — she recognizes Noor from a file that officially doesn't exist. Cold, professional, oddly nostalgic. Beat: menace with intimacy.

chapters.title: Terms of Extraction
chapters.summary: Noor agrees to take Voss's case, negotiating terms like a hostage exchange — with Voss as both client and collateral. Beat: reluctant commitment, the negotiator negotiating herself into danger.

chapters.title: First Border
chapters.summary: A tense crossing by train; Noor talks a border inspector down using pure technique while Voss hides in plain sight. Beat: triumph shadowed by the realization someone tipped off the inspection.

chapters.title: What the Photograph Showed
chapters.summary: Noor confronts Voss with the photo; he admits the 'favor' happened during the Lisbon failure — Noor spared him without knowing it, and someone drugged the memory away. Beat: vertigo of self-doubt.

chapters.title: Sable Closes Distance
chapters.summary: Sable's POV as she eliminates a middleman and leaves a message only Noor would understand — a phrase from the erased night. Beat: psychological pressure replacing physical threat.

chapters.title: The Agency That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Noor tracks the unit that wiped their memory through a retired handler who drinks too much and remembers too much. Learns the erasure was traded for Noor's life. Beat: betrayal of one's own mind.

chapters.title: Second Border
chapters.summary: A botched safehouse handoff forces Noor and Voss into a night flight through mountains; Adeyemi's team nearly takes them. Beat: trust forged under fire between two strangers bound by a false memory.

chapters.title: Adeyemi's Doubt
chapters.summary: Adeyemi's POV. Ordered to bury the evidence unread, she reads it instead — and finds her own government's signature on the massacre order. Beat: conscience igniting inside the machine.

chapters.title: The Negotiation With Herself
chapters.summary: Noor, cornered, weighs trading Voss's evidence for restoration of her own name and records. The old hunger to matter again versus the truth she now carries. Beat: moral nadir.

chapters.title: Third Border
chapters.summary: The final crossing into the summit city; Sable ambushes the convoy but lets Noor live, demanding answers about the night they both survived. Beat: enemy revealed as witness.

chapters.title: Two Survivors
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She was the other person in the room the night of Lisbon; the massacre's first casualty was her own squad, and she was ordered to forget too. Uneasy alliance forms. Beat: shared wound.

chapters.title: The Summit Convenes
chapters.summary: Delegations arrive; security locks down; Adeyemi must decide whether to report Noor's location or lose her thread of the truth forever. Beat: converging clocks.

chapters.title: Hostage to the Truth
chapters.summary: When officials seize Voss, Noor does what she does best: walks into the room and negotiates — this time with three governments as the hostage-takers. Beat: full command of her craft, highest stakes.

chapters.title: Everything on the Table
chapters.summary: Climax. The evidence goes live mid-session; Sable holds the hall at gunpoint not to kill but to be heard; Adeyemi chooses to corroborate rather than contain. Beat: catharsis through exposure.

chapters.title: The Price of Being Seen
chapters.summary: Aftermath begins: governments scramble, Voss vanishes as couriers do, and Noor faces arrest, immunity, or exile depending on which version of events holds. Beat: bittersweet cost accounting.

chapters.title: Restoration
chapters.summary: Noor testifies, reclaiming the Lisbon night in full — including the life she saved and the one she couldn't. The record is corrected; the failure stays on the board, honestly hers. Beat: integration of grief and identity.

chapters.title: Attributed
chapters.summary: Final chapter. Noor, publicly named at last, takes a case everyone wants attributed — and finds Voss's calling card inside the file: another favor, another debt, another door open. Beat: belonging found in being seen, with the future unwritten.
